subject: design-technology

moments.title: Phoebus cartel formed
moments.who: Osram, Philips, GE and others, Geneva
moments.body:
Major bulb manufacturers agree to limit incandescent lamp lifetimes to around 1,000 hours, down from approximately 2,500.

The cartel introduces fines for members exceeding the target.
moments.takeaway: Planned obsolescence is documented in legal records, not just inferred.

moments.title: Vance Packard's The Waste Makers
moments.body: Packard's book popularises 'planned obsolescence' as a critique of American consumer culture.
moments.takeaway: Public-facing critique gave the practice a name.

moments.title: EU right-to-repair framework
moments.body: The Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation enters into force, with sector-specific delegated acts requiring spare parts, repair access and information.
moments.takeaway: Regulation now reshapes design constraints that were once left to manufacturers.

now.title: Sustainable design today
now.body: Lifecycle assessment, embodied carbon and product passports become standard parts of design briefs in many sectors.
now.open_questions: How are design metrics standardised across global supply chains? Does longevity compete with energy efficiency?

reflection: What earlier designers treated as a sales strategy is now treated by lawmakers as an environmental harm.
